# Expected output SHAPE for s04 (human-in-the-loop approval gating).
#
# The demo is offline and deterministic — it plays a fixed batch of tool calls
# through the ApprovalGate, so this IS reproducible (modulo the temp path).
#
# `go run .` (default: injected approver REJECTS escalations):
#
#   [s04] workspace=/tmp/s04-demo-XXXX approveAll=false approveYes=false interactive=false
#   [gate] read_file   path="notes.txt"     -> auto-approve ran=true
#          tool_result(call_1, is_error=false): hello from the workspace
#   [gate] write_file  path="out.txt"       -> auto-approve ran=true
#          tool_result(call_2, is_error=false): wrote 22 bytes to out.txt
#   [gate] write_file  path="../escape.txt" -> reject       ran=false
#          tool_result(call_3, is_error=true): The user rejected the "write_file" tool call. Feedback: rejected by injected approver
#
# What to verify you ran it correctly:
#   1. read_file  -> auto-approve, ran=true      (read-only is pre-cleared, no prompt)
#   2. write_file out.txt -> auto-approve, ran=true   (in-workspace write pre-cleared by path)
#   3. write_file ../escape.txt -> reject, ran=false  (escaping path escalates; injected human rejects)
#   4. the rejected call still produces a tool_result with is_error=true
#      (a rejection round-trips as FEEDBACK to the model, it does NOT abort)
#
# Flags that change the shape:
#   go run . -y            # injected approver APPROVES → call_3 runs (ran=true)
#   go run . -approve-all  # policy pre-clears everything → call_3 auto-approve
#   go run . -i            # ask Y/N on stdin for the escaping write
#
# Tests are fully offline and need no flags:
#   GOWORK=off go test -count=1 ./...
